title: The Day South Korea Lost Its Digital Memory
objective: Explain what happened when a battery fire at a South Korean government data center in September 2025 took down hundreds of public systems and permanently destroyed the 858 TB G-Drive, and what the episode shows about backups and putting everything in one building.
audience: General viewers on short-form platforms; no knowledge of data centers, cloud storage or Korean government IT assumed.

message.core_message: One fire in one server room erased eight years of government work, because the biggest drive was too large to back up and sat in the same building as everything it served.
key_points: 26 September 2025: a battery fire at the National Information Resources Service (NIRS) data center in Daejeon, South Korea, during a UPS battery relocation
96 core systems were directly damaged; 647 systems were affected in total, many shut down pre-emptively; public services from ID and postal to tax and welfare went offline
G-Drive, the government's shared cloud storage, held 858 TB and had no backup: officials said its size made backup impractical
Most other systems were backed up daily in-building and at a remote site, so they could be restored
Recovery was gradual: about 18% of affected systems in the first week, roughly 90% by end of October, Daejeon fully restored in mid-November (figures to confirm in research)
Police booked four people on suspicion of professional negligence; the lesson is redundancy, tested backups and battery safety

avoid: a single unsourced number stated as settled where sources disagree
the unverified claim that the fire disrupted 'more than 160' services: reporting says 647 systems, so use the sourced figure
blaming named individuals or implying guilt before any court finding
fake news-channel graphics, breaking-news banners or red-alert HUDs
gore, panic imagery or real people's faces
glowing node diagrams, matrix rain, generic hacker aesthetics

constraints: Light canvas throughout; loss reads through scorching, fading and erasure, not a dark background
Every number on screen carries its source or its range where sources disagree (647 systems vs 709 services; 858 TB is G-Drive only)
Distinguish 'directly burned' (96 systems) from 'shut down as a precaution' (the rest)
No generated imagery is presented as real footage or photography; no logos of real agencies or companies
Portrait only unless more formats are requested (docs/VISION.md default)
Narration states reported figures as reported and the cause as under investigation unless research shows a finding

audio.notes: Restrained bed at about -26 dBFS; low server-room hum that cuts out when the fire starts; no whooshes on dissolves; no alarm stings. Voice: documentary male voice via src/pipeline/tts.py; pick and speed during voice-director.

research.reason: Current-events claims with disagreeing counts (647 systems vs 709 services, 125,000 vs 750,000 G-Drive users), a user-supplied '160+ services' figure that sources do not support, and a cause and liability that were under investigation.

creative_directions.name: Filing cabinet burns out
creative_directions.concept: The film is a grid of paper folder tabs and ID cards laid on an off-white desk, each labelled with a public service (ID, tax, post, welfare, courts). A single warm ember appears in one corner of the server room drawing at the edge of the frame, and a scorch front crawls across the grid: tabs curl, brown at the edge and fall away to bare paper. The 858 TB drive is one large folder at the centre that burns with no duplicate beneath it, contrasted with other folders whose ghost copies glide to a remote shelf and survive. The end is a recovery tally filling slowly, with an empty folder still left.

visual_identity.palette: off-white #F5F3EF, charcoal #24211E, vermilion #D9432B for the fire and counts, marigold #E8A93B for warmth and ember, ultramarine #2B4FA3 for restored systems, ash grey #8C877F
visual_identity.typography: Playfair Display for titles and big numbers, Inter for support lines, JetBrains Mono for system names and dates
visual_identity.texture: paper grain, scorch edges via displaced masks, soft ash particles

motion_language.personality: calm and exact until the burn, then relentless; recovery is slow and stepped
signature_moves: scorch front crossing a tab grid
ghost copy sliding to a remote shelf
tally counter filling toward but not reaching full
motion_language.transitions: the burn carries scene to scene as a continuous element; dissolves on shared paper; no whooshes

composition.approach: Portrait: the grid occupies the upper two-thirds inside the safe area, one line of support copy sits below it above the bottom UI zone, the central 858 TB folder anchors the middle.

creative_directions.pacing: new picture or beat every 2-3 s; scenes 8-12 s each; the final hold is 3 s
creative_directions.why_it_fits: Delivers the brief's hook of records, services and identities vanishing as the building burns, keeps the canvas light, and makes backup versus no backup visible in one image.

creative_directions.name: Cutaway server building
creative_directions.concept: An isometric cross-section of the Daejeon building in thin line art with racks per floor, each rack lit by the service it runs. The fire starts in the battery area and rises floor by floor, racks going grey as service icons drop out of a city skyline above. A second small building labelled 'remote backup' receives arrows from every rack except one.

signature_moves: arrow draw-on to the backup site

composition.approach: tall building cross-section suits portrait, with a skyline of services at the top

creative_directions.pacing: a rack or service every 2 s
creative_directions.why_it_fits: Explains the mechanism clearly, but drifts toward the glowing-diagram look the project avoids and carries less emotional weight.

success_criteria: Every on-screen figure matches research.json including disagreements between sources
The hook (records, services and identities disappearing as the facility burns) lands inside the first 10 s
Visible change at least every 3 s while narration speaks
The viewer can state afterwards why G-Drive was lost while other systems recovered
